frameTime.probe: tests/narcosis.spec.js, 'a frame with every narcosis effect on takes no longer than one without': two pages resume the same dive at 20 m, one at index 0.94 (all four effects on throughout: still above 0.45 at its last frame), one at 0, both holding a fin key and the vent. Frames are stepped by hand; each sample is one frame's real time with gl.finish(), so the GPU's work (SwiftShader, 960x540 at DPR 1 in headless Chromium) is included. 30 warm-up frames each, then 6 interleaved rounds of 50, 300 samples each. The assertion: narcosed median <= sober median * 1.25 + 0.5 ms.

frameTime.reading: Alone, the medians agree within 0.3 ms, three of four within 0.1 ms. The p95 and maximum swing both ways between runs (5.6 against 14.9, 37.9 against 25.3) and are the machine's, not the effects'. Under the suite's load the medians differ by 0.3 and 0.9 ms. Legacy's ctx.filter blur and grayscale, which this slice does not port, are what made performance collapse (owner, #220).

rule: Owner decision on #220 (2026-10-07): the tunnel vision above index 0.15 is one pre-rendered overlay sprite whose alpha follows the index, with no per-frame gradient; the wobble above 0.25 is an offset of the world container, on the scene's real-time clock; blur and grayscale are not ported, recorded in docs/decisions.md as a deliberate departure. The wobble is off under prefers-reduced-motion (docs/decisions.md, Accessibility: reduced-motion support).
change: src/render/narcosis-view.ts holds legacy's vignette alpha, min(0.7, (index - 0.15) * 0.82), and wobble, sin(t * 0.002) * str across and cos(t * 0.0015) * str * 0.5 down with str = (index - 0.25) * 8 px, t in ms of the scene's elapsedRealS. src/render/pixi-renderer.ts draws legacy's radial gradient (clear at 0.3 of the shorter side, black at 0.7 of the longer) on a canvas once per viewport size, as one sprite over the world and not moved by the wobble; each frame sets its alpha and visibility from PresentationState.narcosisIndex and offsets the world container by the wobble, unless prefers-reduced-motion is set. scripts/pixi-visual-check.mjs adds wreck-narcosis, a dive resumed from its own first save at 20 m, index 0.9, frames pinned. docs/decisions.md records blur and grayscale as a deliberate departure.

counterChecks.method: Each mutation applied by a script to a file backed up beforehand, the client rebuilt, the named checks run under the port lock with --retries=0, then the file restored from its backup and compared with filecmp (shallow=False): byte for byte identical in every case, and the client rebuilt. The first forms of V3 and V5 did not typecheck, so their builds failed before any check ran; the results below are from the typechecking forms, (this.#reducedMotion?.matches && false) and wobble.x * 0.
